clue.text: Dullest dullard overwhelmed by exam

indicators.note: something overwhelmed is swamped on every side, so the dullard sits wrapped inside the exam

blocks.note: an exam is a test
a hick is an unsophisticated country bumpkin

explanation.surface: The slowest student in the class is swamped by an examination paper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dullest' and 'dullard' look like a repeated idea, but only the first is the definition; the second supplies the bumpkin inside the test.
explanation.definitionFit: Thick is informal for stupid, so the superlative form describes the most slow-witted person around.

clue.text: Soften, harden

blocks.note: first meaning: to moderate or tone down
second meaning: to toughen steel by heating and cooling it

explanation.walkthrough: The two definitions are opposites, which makes the clue look self-contradictory until you find one verb carrying both senses.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to mitigate something, and in metalwork it means toughening steel through controlled heating and quenching.

clue.text: Telling off about part of Bible having been ripped off

indicators.note: off here means gone bad or awry, so the letters of the first word are spoiled into a new order
about means surrounding, so the shuffled letters go around the scriptural part

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
OT is the Old Testament, one part of the Bible

explanation.surface: Someone is scolded over a stolen portion of a Bible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Telling off' reads as a scolding, but it splits into fodder and an anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods obtained by theft or dishonest means are described as acquired wrongfully, which is what stolen loot is.

clue.text: 'Back off: yes? No?': Europe to UK, confused

indicators.note: confused means muddled up, so the preceding words are jumbled into a fresh order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Brexit-era exchange: the EU tells Britain to stop interfering while Britain dithers between yes and no.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom tells someone to stop prying into another's business, the same as telling them to withdraw.

clue.text: Impudence. Boy on Sabbath's clothing: comfy shoes

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed above, so the boy sits on top of the day
clothing means dressing or wrapping, so the boy and day go around the impudence

blocks.note: lip is cheeky talk
a son is a boy
S abbreviates Sunday, the Christian Sabbath

explanation.surface: A cheeky lad dresses casually on a Sunday, wearing comfortable footwear.
explanation.walkthrough: Boy and Sabbath make SONS, which is split open to take LIP after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Shoes without laces or fastenings that are simply pushed onto the feet are easy, comfortable footwear.

clue.text: Fish by river, finding one gliding on surface

indicators.note: by means next to, so the river abbreviation is set beside the fish

blocks.note: a skate is a flat fish related to the ray
R is the standard abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: An angler by a river spots someone gliding over the frozen water.
explanation.definitionFit: A person on blades or wheels moves smoothly across ice or pavement, gliding over a surface.

clue.text: Observe horny suitor fumbling: 'Cool it!'

indicators.note: fumbling means handling clumsily, so the two words are mishandled into a new order

blocks.note: to observe a rule or custom is to keep it
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Watching an eager admirer grope clumsily, someone tells him to calm down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Observe' looks like an instruction to watch, but it means keep, as in keeping a rule.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are idioms telling someone to calm down and stop getting worked up or angry.

clue.text: Every so often, third yawl finds a kind of large wave

definitions.note: the answer is the adjective that describes this kind of wave

indicators.note: every so often means at regular intervals, so only every other letter of the phrase is kept

blocks.note: the first, third, fifth, seventh and ninth letters

explanation.surface: A third small sailing boat meets a huge wave now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: A yawl is a two-masted sailing boat; the words are just a letter source.
explanation.definitionFit: A tidal wave is a very large ocean wave, so the adjective names that kind of wave.

clue.text: Naughty, vandalising cars with mate

indicators.note: vandalising means wrecking, so the vehicles are smashed into a different order

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
a mate or friend is an ally

explanation.surface: Mischievous youths smash up cars alongside a friend.
explanation.definitionFit: A rascal is a mischievous person, so behaviour like a rogue's is impish and badly behaved.

clue.text: Workers' groups' stewards initially rising to show agreement

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word it follows
in a down clue rising means moving upward, so the letter climbs from the end into the middle

blocks.note: a trade union is a workers' group; its plural S is the letter that moves
first letter of stewards

explanation.surface: Union shop stewards stand up together to show solidarity.
explanation.walkthrough: Workers' groups gives UNIONS; its final S, standing for stewards, rises two places up the down entry to give UNISON, itself a big British public-sector union.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting in unison means acting together in perfect accord, so the word stands for harmony or concord.

clue.text: Entertaining literature: primarily, a deep source?

definitions.text: Entertaining literature: primarily, a deep source?

indicators.note: entertaining means playing host to, so the source holds the selected letter inside
primarily means first of all, so only the opening letter of literature is kept

blocks.note: a mine is a deep source of minerals
first letter of literature

explanation.surface: Light reading is, above all, a rich source of something.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the author: A A Milne, creator of Winnie-the-Pooh, is a deep source of entertaining literature.
explanation.definitionFit: Alan Alexander Milne wrote the Winnie-the-Pooh stories, a well of much-loved children's writing.

clue.text: Hints end in sight amid unions' disruption

indicators.note: amid means in the middle of, so one word is placed inside the other
disruption throws things into disorder, so the letters are scrambled

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
the word end, plainly visible, goes in as written

explanation.surface: There are signs that the strikes and industrial unrest are nearly over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In sight' reads as part of the strike news; it just says the word end is there to be seen and used.
explanation.definitionFit: Innuendos are indirect suggestions or insinuations, remarks that imply rather than state outright.

clue.text: Giving a name to mouse-pony hybrid

indicators.note: a hybrid is a cross mixing two sources, so the letters of both animals are mixed together

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A cross between a rodent and a small horse names something after itself.
explanation.definitionFit: An eponymous figure is the person or thing after whom something, such as a title or place, is called.

clue.text: Year on island, topless resort

indicators.note: on means placed against, so the year abbreviation is set beside the island
topless means without its top, so the island loses its opening letter

blocks.note: Y is the abbreviation for year
Malta is a Mediterranean island

explanation.surface: A year spent on a Mediterranean island at a resort where sunbathers go topless.
explanation.walkthrough: Yalta is a Black Sea resort in Crimea, famous for the 1945 conference.
explanation.definitionFit: This Crimean town on the Black Sea coast is a well-known holiday destination.

clue.text: In conclusion, Guinness sells these!

indicators.note: in conclusion points to the closing letter of the brand name

blocks.note: last letter of Guinness
to tout is to sell or peddle

explanation.surface: A summing-up: these are what the Irish brewery Guinness sells.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: Guinness is the famous Irish brand of dark beer.
explanation.definitionFit: Stouts are strong dark beers brewed with roasted malt, and Guinness is the best-known example.

clue.text: Impartial head of Ireland ignored in new EU test

indicators.note: the opening letter of Ireland is left out from within the word for test

blocks.note: N is the abbreviation for new
taken as written
a trial is a test

explanation.surface: Ireland's leader is left out of a fresh European Union assessment, despite being even-handed.
explanation.definitionFit: Being neutral means taking no side in a dispute, which is what impartial means.

clue.text: Energy lost from dodgy rear heater's element

indicators.note: lost from means taken away, so one letter is dropped from the words that follow
dodgy means unreliable or faulty, so the letters come out in a broken order

blocks.note: E is the physics symbol for energy
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A faulty heater in the back of a car loses power because of one component.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Element' suggests a heating element in the surface, but it means a chemical element.
explanation.definitionFit: Rare earths are a group of metallic chemical elements, the lanthanides, so one of them is an element.

clue.text: 'Happy, Sir?' (Man, unfortunately, is furious)

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things gone wrong, so the letters fall into a muddled order

blocks.note: up means cheerful, as in feeling up
taken as written, to be rearranged
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone asks a gentleman if he is content, but sadly the man is livid.
explanation.definitionFit: Being up in arms is an idiom for being angrily protesting or indignant about something.

clue.text: Consume fruitcake with a bit of salad

blocks.note: to pine is to waste away, as consumption consumes a sufferer
fruitcake and nut are both slang for a crazy person

explanation.surface: Someone eats fruitcake along with a little salad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Consume' looks like eating, but it is intransitive here: to be consumed with grief, wasting away.
explanation.definitionFit: These small edible seeds from pine cones are often scattered over salads as a garnish.

clue.text: Second-rate chump has to return prize

indicators.note: to return means to go back, so the word for chump is read backwards

blocks.note: a nit is a fool
a pot is slang for a trophy cup

explanation.surface: An inferior fool is made to hand back his award.
explanation.definitionFit: Tin-pot describes something petty, shoddy or inferior, a common term of disparagement for mediocrity.

clue.text: Stingy; losing pound will get you grief

indicators.note: losing means giving up, so the currency symbol is dropped from the word for stingy

blocks.note: miserly means mean with money
L, from Latin libra, is the symbol for a pound

explanation.surface: A tightwad who loses a pound is heartbroken.
explanation.definitionFit: Misery is great unhappiness or distress, the same as deep sorrow.

clue.text: Endless acrimony with development for island

indicators.note: endless means without its end, so the final letter is cut off
development means growing into something new, so the letters are reshaped

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Unending bitterness over building development on a holiday island.
explanation.walkthrough: Minorca, or Menorca, is one of Spain's Balearic Islands.
explanation.definitionFit: Minorca is a Mediterranean island in the Balearic group off the east coast of Spain.

clue.text: Hindu creator's not a creator of music

indicators.note: not means without, so the following word is removed from the god's name

blocks.note: Brahma is the creator god of Hinduism, with the possessive S
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Hindu creator god is said not to be a composer.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue repeats creator to make the two figures seem alike, but one is a god and the other the German composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Johannes Brahms was a German Romantic composer, so he made symphonies and other works.

clue.text: Half of theological colleges regressive in Languedoc city

indicators.note: half of means only one of two equal parts is kept and the rest discarded
regressive means going backwards, so the kept letters are read in the opposite direction

blocks.note: seminaries train priests and ministers

explanation.surface: Some theological schools in a southern French region are going backwards.
explanation.walkthrough: Languedoc is a region of southern France; Nîmes is its Roman city.
explanation.definitionFit: Nîmes is a historic city in the Languedoc region of southern France, known for its Roman arena.

clue.text: Following agreement, I'm reversing position

indicators.note: following means coming after, so the next word is placed after the first
reversing means going backwards, so the combined letters are read in the opposite direction

blocks.note: a nod signals agreement
taken as written

explanation.surface: Having reached a deal, someone changes their stance.
explanation.walkthrough: Mid-on is a cricket fielding position, in front of the batsman on the leg side.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket, mid-on is a place where a fielder stands, close to the bowler on the leg side.

clue.text: Having branches cut back to make room for using the net

indicators.note: back means turned round, so the verb for cut is read backwards
making room for something means opening up a space for it inside

blocks.note: to cut, as in cut along, is to run away; ran is the past tense
being online means connected to the internet

explanation.surface: Trees are pruned to clear space for a cable or a fishing net.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Branches cut back' looks like pruning, but branches belongs to the definition and cut back is the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Something not in a straight line, like a branching structure or narrative, does not proceed in a single sequence.

clue.text: Arid broadcast from our station

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, as seed is sown, so the letters are spread into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
of can mean from, as in a man of Kent
taken as written

explanation.surface: A dry, dull programme goes out from the local station.
explanation.walkthrough: Radio Four is the BBC's national speech radio station; 'broadcast' fits the surface but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: BBC Radio 4 is a national British speech-based radio service, so it is a broadcasting outlet.

clue.text: Primarily, text orthodox rabbi always honours?

definitions.text: Primarily, text orthodox rabbi always honours?

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so only the opening letters of the following words are kept

blocks.note: first letters of the five words

explanation.surface: Above all, which scripture does an orthodox rabbi always revere?
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also defines the answer: the Torah is the text an orthodox rabbi honours above all.
explanation.definitionFit: The Torah, the first five books of the Hebrew Bible, is the central scripture of Judaism.

clue.text: Father Christmas, catching cold, retreats

indicators.note: catching means taking hold of, so Father Christmas encloses the abbreviation

blocks.note: Santa is another name for Father Christmas
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: Santa Claus, having caught a chill, withdraws to rest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retreats' looks like a verb for Santa withdrawing, but it is the plural noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A sanctum is a private room or place of refuge, and sancta is its Latin plural.

clue.text: Drinks Australian ingested, displaying signs of overindulgence

indicators.note: ingested means swallowed, so the abbreviation ends up inside the drinks

blocks.note: punches are mixed fruit drinks, often alcoholic
A is the abbreviation for Australian

explanation.surface: An Australian downing drinks begins to show a beer belly.
explanation.definitionFit: Paunches are large protruding stomachs, which come from eating and drinking too much.
